tei:div.tei:ab: 17. X. Zur Urlinie in Beethoven op. 10 No 1; Chopin Etude op. 25 No 2, Fmoll, T. 1–4.
3. XI. Fortsetzung des Fingersatzes der Etude.Diary November 3: “Hoboken: ‘I have arranged for you to be paid for two months.’ I reply: ‘As you wish.’”
5. XI. Zurück zum 2-stimmigen Satz, 1. Gattung; viele Aufgaben korrigiert.

14. X. XI.
Urlinie u. Spiel vereinigt.

17. X. XI.
Mozart Sonate Adur, neu; Urlinie des Themas, Spiel
der T. 1–4.
19. XI. Dreistimmger Satz, Beantwortung mehrerer Fragen.
21. XI. Ueber Solmisation; Mozart, Thema fortgesetzt.
17. XII. Aufgaben im zwei- u. dreistimmigen Satz korrigiert.

24. XII. Zur 2. Gattung des dreistimmigen Satzes.A long entry in Schenker’s diary for December 24, 1925, includes: “Hoboken arrives for his lesson (!), finds the candles "very nice" – soon the electricity is working again, at least a part of it; we work during the lesson by electric light. [...]”
14. I. Etwas zur Gmoll-Sinfonie von Mozart u. zur Cmoll-Sinfonie von Beethoven.
16. I. Chopin Etude Fdur, op. 10 No ?, neu.
23. I. Urlinie dieser Etude fortgesetzt, dann gespielt.
26. I. Mozart Menuett; versucht eine Urlinie u. Fingersatz.
28. I. Dritte Gattung des dreistimmigen Satzes, Aufgaben im zwei- u. dreistimmigen Satz.
6. II. Schubert Walzer op. 9,These pieces were published as 36 Originaltänze by Diabelli around 1822. Urlinie des ersten Walzers korrigiert.
11. II. Schubert WalzerThese pieces were published as 36 Originaltänze by Diabelli around 1822. No 2, korrigiert Urlinie.
13. II. Etude Fdur abgeschlossen u. gespielt.
18. II. Schubert WalzerThese pieces were published as 36 Originaltänze by Diabelli around 1822. No 3, 4 korrigiert (statt Kontrapunkt-Aufgaben).
20. II. Selbst verfertige Uebungen zur Fdur-Etude korrigiert; über Beethoven VII. Sinfonie (Konzert Breisach).
6. III. Menuett abgeschlossen.Diary March 6: “Hoboken is travelling to Munich, will return only after a week.”

16. III. Bringt den Erstdruck der Partita von Seb. BachOf the six partitas for keyboard by Bach (BWV 825–830), Schenker studied the first of these, in B major, most intensively with Elias and Brünauer, in conjunction with the analysis of Beethoven’s Piano Sonata in B, Op. 106. u. Orgel-Fantasien; zeigt den Versuch einer Urlinie der Sarabande.Most probably the Sarabande from the C major Suite for solo cello, which Casals performed at one of his concerts in Vienna and which Schenker assigned to other students (Elias, Brünauer) as an analysis project.
18. III. Synkopen im dreistimmigen Satz; zeigt einen Erstdruck Couperin.

20. III. Ueber die Cello-Sonate Adur (Casals); zu Stravinksys Konzert.Diary March 20: “Hoboken brings Stravinsky's concerto and a few remarks by Fock in the program booklet. I shall keep the concerto at my place for a while.” (Schenker was to use this piece as a counter-example of contrapuntal practice, in the second Meisterwerk Yearbook.)

23. III. Kritik des Casals-Vortrags;Diary March 23: “Hoboken shows me the passages in which he has noted variants or mistakes in Casals's playing; an elegant piece of work.” – Schenker’s diary for March 22 records the concert in an extended description: “Concert: Casals (with Schulhof): Beethoven’s Sonata Op. 69 falls flat! […] a prelude by Moór […] the C major Solo Suite […] two pieces by Schumann “Langsam” and “Mit Humor” […] a sonata by Breval.” Hoboken zeigt seine Notizen, die er während Casals Spiel in sein Stundenbüchlein eingetragen – eine schöne Leistung.

25. III. Fünf-
-te Gattung des zweistimmigen Satzes.

30. III. Ueber die Matthäus-Passion (Klenau); Diary March 27 gives a long description of Klenau’s performance of the St. Matthew Passion, which was broadcast on the radio on that date. alla turka begonnen.
1. IV. Fortsetzung der 5. Gattung u. Synkopen im dreistimmigen Satz.

10. IV. Türkischer Marsch zuende.Diary April 10: “Hoboken appears for his lesson and arrives at 7:30 with Vrieslander for supper. No flowers! The guests stay until 1 a.m., have enjoyed a good meal and good conversation, and ought to have been satisfied.”
13. IV. Bei Rothberger zur Jause.Diary April 13: “3:30 to 5 o'clock at Rothberger's with Vrieslander and Hoboken.”
15. IV. Schubert Walzer,These pieces were published as 36 Originaltänze by Diabelli around 1822. Bilder korrigiert.
17. IV. Versuch Haydn Sonate Gmoll, Entwurf, Fingersatz begonnen.
20. IV. Haydn abgesetzt in Ermanglung einer geeigneten Vorlage; statt dessen Beethoven op. 14 No 2.
29. IV. Aufgaben der Mischungsgattung; Bruckners VII. Sinfonie nachhause genommen, zur Vorbereitung.
5. V. Bruckners VII. Sinfonie, 1. Satz gespielt.Diary May 5: “With Hoboken, Bruckner's Seventh Symphony played four-hands.”
6. V. Mischungsgattung fortgesetzt; Bemerkungen zur Leonoren-Ouvertüre 3.
25. V. Einiges zu Mozart Don Juan; Synthesen Behelfe aus Mendelssohns Schottischer Sinfonie.

27. V. Mozart Sinfonie 1. Satz gezeigt; Fehler in den Partituren; rege die Facsimilerung an.Diary May 27: “I advise Hoboken to save the autograph manuscript of Mozart’s G minor Symphony by having a facsimile edition made. He takes this opportunity to mention an edition of the parts that he obtained a month ago; I ask him to let me see it.” (The symphony in question is identified in the lesson notes for May 29.)

29. V. Bringt neuerworbene Stimmen zur Gmoll-Sinfonie, ältester Druck bei Andrée, ein seltenes Beispiel genauester Wiedergabe der Handschrift; zeigt auch den Erstdruck von Mozarts Hmoll-Adagio u. seines selbständigen Haydn-Andante, das ich aber für unecht erkläre; zeige Stimmführungen in Händels Leçons, Bdur u. in den Variationen; Stimmführungszüge auch in Bachs Emoll-Fuge.Diary May 29: “Hoboken brings the first edition of the parts, published by André, which – a very rare case – show a close agreement with the autograph; in addition, he shows me the first edition of a piano work by Haydn, which I take to be a falsely attributed work, then the Adagio in B minor by Mozart (my first edition is better); finally he shows me a passage from a letter from Vrieslander [...]”
1. VI. Zeige Fehler in Mozarts Sinfonie Fehler in den Partituren.

5. VI. Erklärt sich bereit, auch die Esdur-Sinfonie facsimilieren zu lassen!Diary June 5: “Hoboken declares himself prepared, on his own, also to have the Symphony in E major published in facsimile, and adds that Deutsch is in favor of its publication; [...]”

January 26 Mozart Minuet[entity-001621]; he attempts an Urlinie, and fingering

2. I. Fortsetzung der Etuden op. 25 u. Walzer Asdur op. ?.
16. I. Mozart Sonate Adur; Chopin Walzer Cismoll.

19. II. Appassionata (sehr gut); Chopin Mazurka Hmoll,Probably the Mazurka in B minor Op. 33, No. 4; Op. 30, No. 2, begins in B minor but gravitates towards F minor and ends in that key. (Schenker would have questioned the tonality of Op. 30, No. 2, as he did the second Scherzo, Op. 31.) It is more difficult to identify the other mazurkas mentioned here. neu; wiederholt Gmoll, Cdur.

7. V. Brahms-Paganini-Variationen 1. u. 2. HeftIn a recommendation of Miss Kahn to Otto Erich Deutsch (I.N. 191-566, August 5, 1930), Schenker remarks: “She plays from memory at one sitting Brahms's Paganini Variations, Chopin's complete Etudes Op. 10 and Op. 25, Beethoven's Op. 106, etc.” – trotz Fehlern eine schöne Leistung; Chopin Walzer Asdur, Cismoll, Fdur wiederholt.

21. V. Chopin Ballade
wiederholt; Bach Gavotte Dm aus einer englischen Suite.

5. VI. Etuden von Chopin, sehr gut,In a recommendation of Miss Kahn to Otto Erich Deutsch (I.N. 191-566, August 5, 1930), Schenker remarks: “She plays from memory at one sitting Brahms's Paganini Variations, Chopin's complete Etudes Op. 10 and Op. 25, Beethoven's Op. 106, etc.” ausgenommen op. 25, No 2.

November 7: Beethoven Op. 10, No. 2; Chopin, Berceuse, short waltz in G major

tei:div.tei:ab: 23. X. (1. Stunde!) Chopin Mazurka op. 56 No 1 (Hdur); op. 50 No 3 (Cismoll), neu.Diary Oct 30, 1925: “In the evening, I work on the two mazurkas for Mrs. Pairamall.”

16. XI. Mazurka Fismoll op. 59 No 3 ganz falsch aufgefaßt, ebenso op. 33 No 2 (Ddur).Diary Nov 16: “Mrs. Pairamall brings Chopin mazurkas in the edition of Gebethner as a present, also Zweig’s Three Daemons to read.”
23. XI. Nocturne Fisdur op. 15 No 2, neu.
30. XI. Mazurka Amoll wiederholt.Chopin wrote four mazurkas in the key of A minor but made extensive analytical notes on only one of these, Op. 17, No.4.

14. XII. Mazurka Hmoll op. 30 No 2 neu; Mazurka Cisdur op. 50 No 2,The C- minor mazurka from Chopin’s Op. 50 is No. 3, not No. 2. But Schenker marks the work as “new,” and he had already marked Op. 50, No. 3, as a new work at Pairamall’s lesson on October 23, 1925. So he may be referring to a different C minor mazurka, or to the Mazurka in A major, Op. 50, No. 2. neu.
28. XII. Nocturne Hdur, Mittelteil, Fingersatz; wiederholt Walzer Cismoll, Mittelteil.
4. I. Nocturne Hdur wiederholt, Etude Gism aus op. 25.
11. I. Etude Cmoll aus op. 10 No 12 wiederholt.
18. I. Wiederholt Etude F dur moll op. 10 No 9; Cdur No 7.
25. I. Etude Fmoll op. 10 u. Urlinie-Fragen im Allgemeinen.
8. II. Schubert Impromptu Esdur wiederholt; Chopin Nocturne Cismoll wiederholt u. Fingersatz.Diary Feb 7, 1926: “I work on Chopin's Nocturne in C minor (for Mrs. Pairamall).”
1. III. Schubert Impromptu Asdur, Trio Cismoll statt Desmoll, Vortrag, namentlich Begleitung.

8. III. Bringt Stücke von Rozizky;Ludomir Różycki (1883–1953), Polish composer, who wrote numerous works for solo piano in traditional 19th-century genres (ballades, fantasy pieces, impromptus, intermezzos, nocturnes, and preludes). – Mrs. Pairamall was herself Polish and Schenker was quite liberal in allowing her to play Polish pieces she brought in. Chopin Mazurka Cismoll mit phrygischem d, neu.Chopin wrote five mazurkas in the key of C minor; from Schenker’s reference to “Phrygian d,” the lowered second step of the C minor scale, one can identify this work as Op. 41, No. 1.

15. III. Ueber Ganche, Frl. Dubois usw.;Édouard Ganche (1880–1945) wrote several books about Chopin, including Frédéric Chopin: sa vie et ses œuvres 1810–1849 (Paris: Mercure de France, 1913). Camille Dubois (née O’Meara, 1825–1907) was born in Paris of Irish parents; she studied with Chopin before becoming a concert pianist. The “Miss Dubois” to whom Schenker refers may have been her daughter or granddaughter. bringt „Belege“; über Casals;Schenker’s diary for March 22, in an extended description, gives: “Casals’s concert (with Schulhof): Beethoven’s Sonata Op. 69 is not performed! […] a Prelude by [Emmanuel] Moór […] [Bach’s] unaccompanied Suite in C minor […] two pieces by Schumann, “Langsam” and “Mit Humor” […], a sonata by Bréval.” Chro-
-matische Fantasie wiederholt bis zum Rezitativ.
19. IV. Chopin-Handschrift zurückerstattet; Chromatische Fuge wiederholt.Diary April 19, 1926: “Mrs Pairamall appears again and pays; I return the Chopin autograph manuscript to her.”
26. IV. Nocturne Hdur op. 9 u. Fisdur op. 15 wiederholt.
13. V. Nocturne Fdur, neu.Diary May 13, 1926: “I give [substitute] lessons in lieu of June 28 to Dr. Brünauer, Miss Mosčisker, and Mrs. Pairamall.”
17. V. Noch einmal Nocturn Cismoll, Mittelpartie.

31. V. Schenkt Litzmanns „Clara Schumann“Berthold Litzmann, Clara Schumann: ein Künstlerleben, 3 vols. (Leipzig, 1902–08). Schenker’s diary for this date records: “Mrs. Pairamall gives us Litzmann's Clara Schumann.”

tei:div.tei:ab: 9. X. Brahms Walzer No 4 Emoll: er liest von , ich –.Diary Oct 9: “At 10 o’clock Weisse brings the prints [...] Finally Weisse asks about the Urlinie in Brahms’s Waltz, Op. 39, No. 4 – that he went astray worries him again – I allay these fears as best as I can.” – This lesson note is undated; the above is the only entry before the second lesson (November 2) that relates to the lesson content, so is editorially posited as the lesson date.

2. XI. Chopin Etude Fmoll op 25 No 2 analysiert; über Urlinie-Züge
als Auskomponierung.Schenker’s diary for November 2, 1925, records: “Weisse recounts that, on the occasion of a performance of a Brahms motet, he has once again looked at our studies of the chorale and has now just begun to understand what I meant at the time by Bach’s special art. Once again, he believes that he must defend the concept of Urlinie against the term “Urlinie progressions” (Urlinie-Züge). It becomes ever clearer to me that he is already lumping together the tonal space (Tonraum) in which the Urlinie moves with the Urlinie as understood in composing-out.”
